title: ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui — AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.
content:
AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications. Built for simplicity and flexibility, it enables seamless integration between AI agents, real time user context, and user interfaces.
Join our Discord → Read the Docs → Go to the AG-UI Dojo → Follow us →
Create a new AG-UI application in seconds:
npx create-ag-ui-app my-agent-app
AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol for agent-human interaction, designed for simplicity & flexibility:
- During agent executions, agent backends emit events compatible with one of AG-UI's ~16 standard event types
- Agent backends can accept one of a few simple AG-UI compatible inputs as arguments
AG-UI includes a flexible middleware layer that ensures compatibility across diverse environments:
- Works with any event transport (SSE, WebSockets, webhooks, etc.)
- Allows for loose event format matching, enabling broad agent and app interoperability
It also ships with a reference HTTP implementation and default connector to help teams get started fast.
AG-UI was developed based on real-world requirements and practical experience building in-app agent interactions.
AG-UI is complementary to the other 2 top agentic protocols
- MCP gives agents tools
- A2A allows agents to communicate with other agents
- AG-UI brings agents into user-facing applications
- 💬 Real-time agentic chat with streaming
- 🔄 Bi-directional state synchronization
- 🧩 Generative UI and structured messages
- 🧠 Real-time context enrichment
- 🛠️ Frontend tool integration
- 🧑💻 Human-in-the-loop collaboration
AG-UI was born from CopilotKit's initial partnership with LangChain and CrewAI - and brings the incredibly popular agent-user-interactivity infrastructure to the wider agentic ecosystem.
1st party = the platforms that have AG‑UI built in and provide documentation for guidance.

report.summary: AG-UI is an open, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to frontend applications, complementing MCP and A2A to complete the agentic stack.
report.background: The agentic AI boom has produced powerful but fragmented infrastructure. Anthropic's MCP standardized how agents access tools, and Google's A2A addressed agent-to-agent communication. Yet a critical gap remained: how agents stream events, state, and generative UI into user-facing applications. Teams often built bespoke, brittle integrations for every frontend. AG-UI emerged from CopilotKit's early partnership with LangChain and CrewAI, distilling real-world in-app agent interaction patterns into a lightweight, open protocol. It defines roughly 16 standard event types, supports any transport like SSE, WebSockets, or webhooks, and uses a flexible middleware layer for loose format matching. Licensed MIT, it aims to bring the popular agent-user-interactivity infrastructure to the wider ecosystem, positioning itself as the missing user-interface layer of the agentic protocol trio.
key_points: Event-based standardization: Agent backends emit events matching one of about 16 standard AG-UI event types and accept simple AG-UI-compatible inputs. The protocol allows loose event format matching, enabling broad interoperability between diverse agents and frontend applications without rigid schemas.

Transport-agnostic middleware: AG-UI works with any event transport, including SSE, WebSockets, and webhooks. A flexible middleware layer ensures compatibility across environments, and the project ships with a reference HTTP implementation and default connector so teams can start quickly.

Core interaction features: The protocol supports real-time agentic chat with streaming, bi-directional state synchronization, generative UI and structured messages, real-time context enrichment, frontend tool integration, and human-in-the-loop collaboration, covering the full range of modern agent-user interactions.

Complements MCP and A2A: AG-UI is designed as the third pillar alongside MCP, which gives agents tools, and A2A, which lets agents talk to each other. AG-UI brings agents into user-facing applications, completing the path from tools to agents to end users.

Fast onboarding and open ecosystem: Developers can scaffold an app with npx create-ag-ui-app, explore core building blocks through the AG-UI Dojo's 50-200 line examples, and follow a public roadmap, Discord, and biweekly working group. The project is MIT-licensed and backed by first-party integrations.
report.impact: For the AI industry, AG-UI fills the last major protocol gap, potentially standardizing how every agent-powered app handles streaming, state, and UI generation. It could reduce vendor lock-in and accelerate agent adoption across consumer and enterprise software. For developers, it means less custom glue code when connecting agent backends to React, mobile, or web frontends, plus freedom to choose transports and frameworks. It also gives frontend teams a clear contract for human-in-the-loop controls and generative UI. For regular users, the payoff is smoother, more responsive agents embedded directly in apps, with real-time feedback, synchronized state, and meaningful intervention points rather than opaque chat boxes. Ultimately, AG-UI could make agent interactions feel like native app features rather than bolted-on experiments.
report.tools: To follow up, start with the create-ag-ui-app CLI (npx create-ag-ui-app) and the AG-UI Dojo for small, focused examples. Watch CopilotKit, the project's originator, plus LangChain and CrewAI for integrations. Compare with MCP for tool access and A2A for agent-to-agent communication. The AG-UI docs, roadmap, Discord, and biweekly working group are key resources. For production, review the reference HTTP implementation, default connector, and supported transports like SSE and WebSockets.
